[[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] were the defending champions, having won their 11th title in the [[2007–08 Saudi Premier League|previous season]]. The campaign began on 13 September 2008 and ended on 12 April 2009. A total of 12 teams contested the league, 10 of which already contested in the 2007–08 season, and two of which were promoted from the [[Saudi First Division League|First Division]]. On 12 April 2009, in the final round of the season, [[Al-Ittihad Club (Jeddah)|Al-Ittihad]] won the title after a 2–1 victory over [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]].{{cite web |title=الاتحاد يتوج بلقب الدوري السعودي على حساب الهلال |url=https://www.aljarida.com/articles/1461736665996235900/}} It was their eighth league title overall. [[Al-Ittihad Club (Jeddah)|Al-Ittihad]], [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]], [[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]] and [[Al Shabab FC (Riyadh)|Al-Shabab]] all secured a berth for the [[2010 AFC Champions League]], while [[Al-Nassr FC|Al-Nassr]] and [[Al-Ettifaq FC|Al-Ettifaq]] qualified for the [[25th GCC Champions League|Gulf Club Champions Cup]]. [[Al-Watani Club|Al-Watani]] and [[Abha Club|Abha]] were relegated to the [[Saudi First Division League]].{{cite web |title=الحزن يسيطر على لاعبي الوطني بعد الهبوط |url=http://www.alriyadh.com/421179}} ==Changes== ===Professional League rebrand=== On 26 May 2008, the [[Saudi Arabian Football Federation|SAFF]] announced that the league would be rebranded as [[Saudi Pro League]]. The changes were based on the criteria introduced by [[Asian Football Confederation|AFC]] President [[Mohammed bin Hammam]] to improve the football standards in Asia.{{cite web |title=دوري المحترفين في آسيا.. الحلم أصبح حقيقة! |url=http://www.alriyadh.com/345500}} The changes also included a website dedicated to recording statistics of the league for the first time. It was also announced that the website would be run by the Saudi Pro League board rather than the SAFF.{{cite web |title=ثوب الاحتراف يزين الدوري السعودي بعد ثلاثة عقود |url=http://www.alriyadh.com/373855}} ===Qualification and Prize money=== The league champions, runners-up and third place as well as the winner of the [[2009 King Cup of Champions|King Cup of Champions]] qualified for the [[2010 AFC Champions League]]. The top eight teams qualified for [[2009 King Cup of Champions|King Cup of Champions]]. Prize money: * First place: 2.5 million Saudi Riyals * Second place: 1.5 million Saudi Riyals * Third place: 1 million Saudi Riyals ==Teams== Twelve teams competed in the league – the top ten teams from the previous season and the two teams promoted from the [[Saudi First Division League]]. The promoted teams were [[Al Raed FC|Al-Raed]] (returning to the top flight after an absence of five years) and [[Abha Club|Abha]] (returning to the top flight after an absence of two years). They replaced [[Al-Tai FC|Al-Tai]] (after seven consecutive years in the top-flight) and [[Al Qadsiah FC|Al-Qadsiah]] (after six consecutive years in the top-flight). ===Stadiums and locations=== {{Location map+ |Saudi Arabia |width=440 |float=right |caption=Locations of teams in the 2008–09 Saudi Professional League |places= {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=18.216944|long=42.505278 |label=[[Abha Club|Abha]]|position=bottom}} {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=21.54333 |long=39.17278 |label=[[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]]
